key_insight: Peridynamic thermo-mechanical simulations identify cracking thresholds in tungsten across base temperatures and cyclic heat fluxes relevant to fusion reactors.
engineering_relevance: Predicting heat-induced cracking can support plasma-facing material screening and component lifetime assessment.
method: Model component-scale thermo-mechanical fracture using CabanaPD.
Simulate cyclic electron-beam exposure at varying base temperatures and heat fluxes.
Track the spatial distribution and temporal accumulation of cracks and damage.
evidence_signal: Simulations informed by JUDITH electron-beam data for recrystallized pure tungsten compare well with experimental damage classifications.
watch_item: Validation described in the abstract covers electron-beam heating, not combined neutron irradiation and plasma exposure.
paper_title: Peridynamic Thermo-Mechanical Modeling of Cracking in Tungsten under Fusion-Relevant Heat Fluxes
